item.title: Fixing 'make' Utility Errors: The Crucial Role of Tabs vs. Spaces in Makefiles
item.description:
“Fixing ‘make’ Utility Errors: The Crucial Role of Tabs vs. Spaces in Makefiles”

Why Does Indentation Matter in Makefiles?

The fundamental structure of a Makefile dictates that the dependencies line must be immediately followed by the recipe (the shell commands to execute). Crucially, every line belonging to a recipe must begin with a hard tab character (\t), not spaces.

To inspect the file content accurately, use terminal commands like cat -e -t -v <makefile_name>. This reveals line endings ($) and explicitly shows tabs as ^I.
